subject: Preflight: Launch health check & blocker escalation (QBR prep)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: Launch health check & blocker escalation (QBR prep)

Team —

Running a short preflight ahead of the QBR readout next week. Goal: give execs a one-slide view of where product + eng stand on the June launch and surface any blockers we need to escalate. Please reply in-thread by EOD today with the four items below for your area: 

- Single-line status (Green/Amber/Red) and % done for the scope we committed to.
- Top 3 risks (one sentence each) and current mitigations.
- ETA to resolve the top risk (date + confidence).
- Any exec-level decision needed (yes/no + what).

I've attached a short preflight_summary.xlsx and the working timeline (timelines_v2.pdf). Please update the risk_log.csv with timestamps where applicable.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: preflight_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet), timelines_v2.pdf (PDF)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: Launch health check & blocker escalation (QBR prep)

Alex —

Status: Amber — Core inference route and the new streaming backpressure handler are functionally complete; integration tests show 85% of target throughput under synthetic load.

Top risks:
1) Load test failure on long-tail sessions causing increased tail latency. Mitigation: roll back to conservative batching profile on canary; infra execs are running an expanded soak this weekend.
2) Two dependent SDK breaking changes (Python/Node) shipped in last sprint; mitigation: patch release in staging tomorrow.
3) Observability gaps for cross-model KV cache hits; mitigation: temporary trace hooks and sampling.

ETA to resolve top risk (load tail): 2027-06-23 (medium confidence)
Exec decision needed: Yes — if tail doesn't improve by 23rd, we should limit canary to dedicated capacity only and delay hosted ramp for 48 hours.

Sharing timelines_v2.pdf in thread. I also updated risk_log.csv with entries for the load test.

Subject: Re: Preflight: Launch health check & blocker escalation (QBR prep)

Quick product update:

Status: Amber — Feature parity for the billing instrumentation and routing rules is at 92%.

Top risks:
- External dependency: Acme's procurement requires a signed T&Cs addendum for usage retention before we enable long-term data retention. Mitigation: Legal has prepared a slim addendum; request procurement signoff by 6/22.
- UX regression in the admin console for multi-tenant routing; mitigation: UX team prioritized a patch, rolling to staging tomorrow.
- Integration gating: Marketplace partner's API version mismatch; mitigation: partner provided a compatibility shim (partner@cloudmarket.com).

ETA to unblock procurement: 2027-06-22 (high confidence)
Exec decision needed: No immediate exec decision, but Legal/Procurement to expedite signoff.

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: Launch health check & blocker escalation (QBR prep)

Heads-up — infra saw an incident in the extended soak last night.

Status: Red for infra stability under long-tail (reproducible at ~1% of sessions).

Details: When KV cache churn increased on long sequences, we saw a memory pressure path that triggers an unexpected GC pause in our runtime on G5-type instances. The pause is short (~200-300ms) but is amplifying tail latency for affected sessions.

Mitigations in flight:
- Backporting a safer cache eviction policy to the runtime (hotfix branch) — CI + canary expected Mon morning.
- Temporary traffic steering: we can route long-tail sessions to a smaller model slice on dedicated capacity as a stopgap.
- Increased observability: heap traces and flamegraphs are being collected and uploaded to the drive folder.

ETA to stabilize hotfix: 2027-06-22 (low/medium confidence)
Exec decision needed: Yes — need permission to restrict hosted canary traffic to dedicated pools until hotfix is validated. This impacts revenue estimates for the first 48 hours of ramp.

Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: Launch health check & blocker escalation (QBR prep)

Monitoring + SRE notes:

Status: Amber — core alerts are firing at lower thresholds and we have a playbook ready.

Top risks:
- Alert fatigue: noise from a new queueing metric is masking the early signal for the GC pause. Mitigation: suppress noisy rule and tune thresholds (in progress).
- Runbook gaps: several steps in the cache-eviction recovery flow aren't automated. Mitigation: pairing with engineering to add a scripted rollback.
- Capacity peak: if we move to dedicated-only canary, capacity ops need 6 hours lead time to spin the bigger pool.

ETA for alert tuning + runbook scripts: 2027-06-21 12:00 (high confidence)
Exec decision needed: No — but ops lead time constraint is important for Alex's escalation.

Cc: Samantha Cole <samantha@acme-fin.com>, Marketplace Partner <partner@cloudmarket.com>, acme-eng@acme-fin.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight: Launch health check & blocker escalation (QBR prep)

Thanks all for the quick updates — appreciate the crisp feeds. Summary and asks for leadership / Acme: 

Summary (one-line): System is functionally ready but infra stability on long-tail sessions is a material blocker for a wide-hosted ramp; recommended posture is a scoped canary on dedicated capacity until hotfix validated.

Immediate asks for execs (Decision required):
1) Approve routing long-tail sessions to dedicated pools only for the initial 48-hour ramp window if the hotfix is not validated by 2027-06-23. Impact: ~48 hrs delay for hosted ramp; routed customers on dedicated pools incur slightly higher unit cost.
2) Approve a proactive notice to Acme: set expectation that long-term retention will require signed addendum by 6/22; product can ship masked pipeline without retention until signed. (Lauren to confirm wording).

Operational notes for Acme and partner (copied):
- We are proactively running a hotfix validation on Mon morning (6/21->6/22). If you see any anomalous tail latency >400ms for long interactions please flag to acme-eng@acme-fin.com and we will prioritize.
- Marketplace partner: thanks for the compatibility shim — please keep the shim available for canary traffic.

Next steps:
- Karthik / Mina to confirm hotfix canary start time (expected Mon 06/21 09:00 PT) and post results.
- Lauren to follow up with Legal/Procurement on addendum signature status by EOD 6/22.
- Grace to finalize alert tuning and runbook scripts by 12:00 6/21.

I'll present this condensed slide in the QBR readout; if the exec group prefers a different posture I need the call by EOD 6/22 so we can adjust the deck and timeline.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: risk_log.csv (CSV of current issues), preflight_summary.xlsx
